Assemble a UKI from a kernel, generated initrd, and boot parameters.

## Inputs

| Name         | Kind | Description                                        |
| ------------ | ---- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `stub`       | file | Systemd EFI stub matching the target architecture. |
| `kernel`     | file | Kernel image to embed.                             |
| `initrd`     | file | Initrd to embed.                                   |
| `cmdline`    | file | Text file containing the kernel command line.      |
| `os-release` | file | OS identification file to embed.                   |

## Outputs

| Name    | Kind | Description                          |
| ------- | ---- | ------------------------------------ |
| `image` | file | Unsigned unified kernel image (UKI). |

## Execution

| Setting      | Value        |
| ------------ | ------------ |
| Environment  | Rugix Bakery |
| Source epoch | Consumed     |
| Output cache | Allowed      |

## Behavior

A Unified Kernel Image (UKI) combines an EFI stub, Linux kernel, initrd,
authenticated command line, and OS identification in one EFI executable. This
rule assembles those explicit inputs with Rugix Bakery's `ukify`. The stub and
kernel must match the target architecture.

The exported `image` is unsigned. Use `core/sign-efi` before deploying it on a
system that enforces UEFI Secure Boot. The command-line and OS identification
inputs are text files.

## Example

For example, assemble prepared boot artifacts:

```toml
uses = "core/uki"
inputs.stub = { path = "boot/stub.efi" }
inputs.kernel = { path = "boot/kernel" }
inputs.initrd = { path = "boot/initrd" }
inputs.cmdline = { path = "boot/cmdline" }
inputs.os-release = { path = "boot/os-release" }
```

Save the invocation as `build-rule.toml` and run
`./run-bakery bake rule build-rule.toml build/result`.
